bull_bear.body: Net cash positive; prioritized DC expansion (₹1,100cr QIP + ₹100cr warrant conversion); zero debt policy maintained; no new debt planned; real estate kept low-leveraged; future capex funded internally
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Cloud demand visibility reliant on govt. data sovereignty laws (pending); MeitY empanelment delayed (expected Nov '25); real estate launch timing risk (Q4 approvals pending); sovereign cloud adoption pace vs. private hyperscalers
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, bullish on DC/cloud trajectory, proud of zero-debt status, emphasizes disciplined execution, avoids forward guidance but confirms all targets are on track, tone is assertive and visionary
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Cloud revenue per MW (₹12cr/month) is 13x Colo's (₹90L/month) — yet same 75% margin, implying massive unit economics advantage; real estate revenue is largely from Anant Raj Estate (legacy) while DC is the future; 8MW vacant capacity in 63MW DC is strategic buffer for Cloud conversion
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Preserve capital discipline: Reinvest operating cash flows and residential real estate proceeds into execution and future land acquisition while pursuing self-funded growth without increasing leverage."
- Platform strength slide states "Net debt-free — As on March 31, 2026"; the deck's Net Debt chart is titled "Reduced Net Debt (₹ Cr)" over FY21-FY26 but the label-to-value binding is not recoverable from the extraction (see notes).
- "Consistent topline growth, healthy margins, and a track record of dividend payouts signals financial strength"; the dividend chart is expressed "As a % of face value" across FY21-FY26, but again the year-to-value binding is lost in extraction.
- The milestone timeline records "Raised Rs.1,100 cr. through QIP" (the specific year cannot be reliably bound from the extracted timeline).
- On the digital platform: "Management has articulated a funded roadmap supported by available funds and future cash flows" for the 357 MW by FY32 end-state.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt-free balance sheet enabling internally funded growth
- Strategic focus on location, permission, and execution as core founding principles
- Established colocation infrastructure providing a foundation for moving up the value chain to sovereign and AI-ready cloud
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Concentration of executive power and family control — The Sarin family (Amit, Aman, Ashim) hold all executive director roles and chair key committees (CSR, Share Transfer, Finance & Investment, Risk Management), creating potential governance and succession risks.
- Business restructuring and demerger execution risk — A Demerger Committee was constituted post-year-end to evaluate restructuring options for the Real Estate and Data Center businesses, introducing uncertainty around operational continuity, capital allocation, and stakeholder impact.
- Real estate sector cyclicality and regulatory risk — As a real estate developer, the Company is exposed to demand cycles, interest rate sensitivity, and evolving regulatory frameworks (e.g., RERA) that can materially impact project viability and cash flows.
- Data center business concentration and technology risk — The strategic pivot into data centers exposes the Company to rapid technological obsolescence, high capital intensity, and dependence on a few large clients or hyperscalers.
- Cyber security risk — The Risk Management Committee explicitly includes cyber security risks in its oversight framework, reflecting the heightened threat landscape for real estate and data center operations.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Describes "5 Decades of Excellence in Real Estate" with presence across 4 key states of India, ~320 acres of prime, debt-free land in Delhi-NCR, 22.34 msf of residential and commercial projects and 2,663 completed units of affordable housing.
- States it upholds "the three core principles: location, permission, and execution", framed as a value-creation flywheel: strategic land, permissions and approvals, disciplined execution, residential plus annuity cash flows, reinvestment and land replenishment.
- Annuity claim: "The portfolio comprises 1.92 million square feet of commercial leasable area, fully leased under long-term agreements, providing strong visibility and stability of cash flows over the extended term."
- On the digital side, claims it is "Strategically Synced with PSUs & Tech Allies" — MeitY empanelment as a Sovereign Cloud Service Provider and BSNL as a Data Centre Service Provider, positioning it to serve government, telecom and enterprise digital infrastructure needs.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] A Composite Scheme of Arrangement has been approved by the Board of Directors to demerge all Data Centre and Cloud operations into Ashok Cloud Pvt. Ltd., creating two independently listed companies — Anant Raj Limited (real estate and infrastructure) and Ashok Cloud (digital infrastructure and cloud services). Stated benefits: greater strategic focus, unlocking shareholder value, and a simplified corporate structure.
- [Demerger — entitlement] "Eligible shareholders will receive 1 equity share of Ashok Cloud (FV ₹2) for every 1 equity share of Anant Raj (FV ₹2) held on the record date."
- [Credit rating] "Infomerics Valuation and Rating Ltd. has upgraded rating of the Company to 'A- Stable' outlook."
- [International] "Established outreach in Singapore by commissioning of Anant Raj Cloud Singapore Pte Ltd for sourcing clients from South East Asia and rest of the world" — described elsewhere as a 100%-owned Singapore subsidiary for international business development.
- [Empanelment / partnerships] Empanelled with MeitY as a Sovereign Cloud service provider and with BSNL as a Data Centre service provider; TIA Tier III certification cited; cloud services delivered "in association with Global Partner" (the partner is not named in the extracted text). A JV with Birla Estate Private Ltd (Birla Navya) covers 191 residential plots planned in 4 phases with 764 luxury independent floors. TARC Ltd was demerged from Anant Raj Ltd in 2020.

Its operations are guided by three core principles: location, permission, and execution.

outlook.body: revenue growth: Data Center to reach ₹1,200cr by FY27; margin: 75% EBITDA margin for DC; order inflow: 63MW by Dec '26, 117MW by FY28; capex/commissioning: ₹700cr total DC capex, 35MW new capacity under development, Rai 20MW by Dec '26, 100MW Greenfield by FY28
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 117MW DC capacity by FY28; Cloud expansion from 14MW to 36MW; SaaS/PaaS layer monetization (revenue doubling potential); 307MW total DC target by FY32; Stellar Resorts redevelopment (7.5M sq.ft.); Delhi commercial entry (7L sq.ft. by FY28)
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Focus on premium and integrated residential developments in NCR, leveraging demand for higher-value homes.
- Expand digital infrastructure portfolio by developing data centres, capitalising on AI, cloud, and digital transformation trends.
- Strengthen commercial real estate presence in NCR, targeting GCCs and technology companies for Grade A office leasing.
- Grow hospitality real estate through sustainability, eco-friendly developments, and experiential accommodation offerings.
- The Board has recommended a final dividend @ 50% i.e. Re. 1 per equity share of Rs. 2 each for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval. The Dividend Distribution Policy is available on the Company's website. During the year, the Company raised Rs. 1,099.99 crores via QIP, of which Rs. 350 crores was utilized towards stated objects and Rs. 750 crores remained unutilized as of March 31, 2026, to be deployed for the purposes for which funds were raised. The Company also redeemed Rs. 22 crores of secured, unlisted, redeemable non-convertible debentures, with Rs. 6.50 crores outstanding as of year-end.
- CSR Committee constituted with defined terms of reference including policy formulation, annual action plans, and performance review; CSR spending reported in Director's Report annexure.
- Risk Management Committee explicitly includes ESG-related risks in its framework for identification of internal and external risks.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Anant Raj Limited is scaling its data centre and cloud services business through a phased capacity build-out. As of March 2026, the Company has operationalised 28 MW IT load across two campuses: Manesar (21 MW) and Panchkula (7 MW). A third campus at Rai, Sonipat, with a planned capacity of approximately 200 MW IT Load, has commenced work and will be operationalised in phases. The Company has also signed an MoU with the Government of Andhra Pradesh for a new 50 MW IT load data centre facility, expanding its footprint into South India. With this addition, total planned data centre capacity reaches 357 MW IT load, of which 117 MW IT load is targeted to commence by FY 2028. The overall roadmap aims to scale capacity to 357 MW by FY 2032. In real estate, the Company is advancing its township development pipeline at Anant Raj Estate, Sector 63A, Gurugram, with multiple phases and group housing projects under construction or in approval stages.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Favourable policy measures, including lower interest rates, GST rationalisation, and continued government focus on housing and infrastructure development, are expected to strengthen affordability, improve liquidity, and support demand in the real estate sector.
- Rising urbanisation, increasing disposable incomes, preference for quality developments, and expanding connectivity infrastructure are expected to drive growth across key markets.
- India's data centre capacity is expected to expand significantly from around 1.5 GW currently to 5-8 GW by 2030, positioning India as a key global hub for cloud, AI, and digital infrastructure investments.
- The hospitality sector is expected to benefit from strong occupancy levels, with pan-India premium hotel occupancy projected to remain at 72-74% in FY 2025-26.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Anant Raj has transformed from a real estate player into a diversified infrastructure giant with Data Centers and sovereign cloud now contributing 28% of H1 FY26 revenue, driven by $1.1B QIP funding and 63MW capacity by Dec '26 — this shift materially de-risks the business and unlocks high-margin recurring revenue streams.
